title: Maximum Projectile Range is Always Achieved at 45 Degrees
statement: The maximum range of any projectile is always achieved when launched at 45 degrees.
incorrect_statement: To maximize projectile distance, always launch at theta = 45 deg.
erroneous_reasoning: Students memorize R = (u^2 sin 2 theta)/g and note that sin(2 theta) is maximized at 2 theta = 90 deg => theta = 45 deg, ignoring the crucial boundary assumption that launch and landing elevations are identical.
why_it_fails: The 45-degree rule applies ONLY to flat, level ground where launch elevation equals landing elevation. When launching from a cliff or onto an incline, the optimal angle shifts significantly.
correct_physics_explanation: When launching from an elevated platform of height h > 0, the projectile spends extra time falling. The optimal launch angle to maximize horizontal range satisfies sin^2(theta_opt) = 1 / [2(1 + gh/u^2)], which is strictly LESS than 45 degrees! Similarly, when projecting up an incline of angle alpha, the optimal angle with the horizontal is theta_opt = 45 deg + alpha/2, which is strictly GREATER than 45 degrees.
corrective_explanation: The 45-degree angle maximizes range strictly on horizontal terrain. When shooting from a cliff, launch at an angle shallower than 45 deg; when shooting uphill, launch steeper than 45 deg.
refutation_counterexample: A shot putter launching from height h = 2 m achieves maximum range at approximately 42 degrees, not 45 degrees.
supporting_evidence: University Physics, Chapter 3: 'Optimal launch angle from a height above ground is always less than 45 degrees.'
diagnostic_symptom: Student automatically substitutes theta = 45 deg into incline range or cliff range optimization problems.
